Section 7. Data Handling and Reporting Requirements

All departments shall maintain a written record of every dataset transferred to a third-party processor. The record shall identify the source system, the date of transfer, the classification of the data, and the name of the receiving organization. Records must be retained for a period of not less than six years and must be made available to the internal audit office upon request.

Any employee who becomes aware of an unauthorized transfer must report the matter to the privacy office within twenty-four hours. The privacy office shall log each report, assign a case number, and notify the general counsel where the transfer involves special category data. Where the matter is referred to a regulator, the privacy office shall keep a copy of all correspondence in the central registry and record the date of closure.

Departments are reminded that consent obtained for one purpose may not be relied upon for another. Where consent is the lawful basis for processing, the department must be able to demonstrate that the data subject was informed of the identity of the controller, the purpose of the processing, and the categories of recipient. Consent must be recorded in the consent management system and reviewed at least once every twelve months, with the review date noted in the register.

Risk assessments shall be completed before any new processing operation begins. The assessment shall describe the nature of the processing, the categories of personal data involved, the duration of the processing, and the technical and organizational measures adopted to mitigate risk. Where the assessment identifies a high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, the department shall consult the supervisory authority before processing begins and shall keep a copy of the response on file.

The compliance team shall prepare a summary of all transfers completed in the preceding quarter, together with any incidents recorded in the register. The quarterly report generated by the compliance team shall be circulated to the board no later than thirty days after the end of each quarter. The report shall include the number of requests received from data subjects, the number resolved within the statutory period, and the number outstanding at the close of the quarter.

Training shall be provided to all staff who handle personal data at least once every two years. Attendance records shall be kept by the learning and development team. Managers shall ensure that new starters complete the introductory module during their first month of employment and that contractors complete an abbreviated version of the same module.

Nothing in this policy limits the rights of data subjects under applicable law. Questions about the interpretation of this policy should be directed to the privacy office, which will publish guidance on the intranet as it is updated and will answer written queries within ten working days.
